Fiona P (arch): quick sync: we keep hitting friction with customers who require IP-level whitelists on private endpoints. debate: per-tenant ENI vs shared ENI + port-mapping/proxying. pros/cons?
Gabe S (neteng): per-tenant ENI gives stable source IPs which customers like. cons: ENI limit, route-table churn, cost.
Hannah T (sre): shared ENI + port mapping (or SNAT pool) worked in past but causes debugging pain when we need to map flows back to tenant. Also flow logs become noisy.
Gabe S (neteng): another variant: per-tenant ephemeral Elastic IPs assigned to NAT instances. Keep small pool and rotate. customers who pin IPs can renew by API.
Fiona P (arch): technical constraints: Dedicated customers can accept per-tenant ENI (they pay), hosted customers prefer shared to save cost. Private deployment customers sometimes run on-prem where ENI semantics differ. Need unified API but different backend implementations.
Hannah T (sre): operational incident from last month: when tenant A hit burst, shared ENI TCP conntrack overflowed and evicted tenant B connections. We need isolation on conntrack and per-tenant quotas.
Gabe S (neteng): option matrix: 
- Option A (per-tenant ENI): stable IP, easier audit, scale limits, cost + route table bloat
- Option B (shared ENI + port map proxy): efficient, simpler infra, bad for whitelists, complex tracing
- Option C (SNAT pools + mapping service): mid cost, requires mapping DB to trace flows, easier to scale via autoscaling NATs
- Option D (user-managed private endpoint in customer VPC): offload IP concerns to customer, but UX worse and onboarding heavy
Fiona P (arch): also consider security groups + source/destination checks. For per-tenant ENI we can apply fine-grained SG rules per tenant which helps compliance.
Gabe S (neteng): perf test idea: simulate 50k concurrent connections across 100 tenants hitting shared ENI vs per-tenant ENI. Measure conntrack failures, flow logs E2E latency, CPU on NAT/proxy nodes. I'll own the spike.
Hannah T (sre): SRE playbook sketch for mitigation if conntrack saturates:
```
- check: kubectl logs nat-proxy | grep conntrack
- immediate: scale up nat-proxy: k scale deploy nat-proxy --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy nat-proxy -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+3)) -n infra
- longer: enable per-tenant conntrack buckets: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=524288
- if IP pinning complaint: create temporary soft-affinity rule and notify customer
```
infra-bot: perf-spike branch test queued (build #4123). ETA 2h. :gear:
Fiona P (arch): UX decision: expose two fields on endpoint create: ip_affinity: ["static","ephemeral","customer-managed"] and ip_ttl_days (for ephemeral). Default: hosted -> ephemeral, dedicated -> static. Private -> customer-managed.
Gabe S (neteng): implementation notes: for ephemeral we need a lease service that hands out IPs and a reconciliation loop that rebinds ENIs on failover. Also need to emit mapping events to audit log.
Hannah T (sre): metrics we need: per-tenant conntrack_usage, nat_pool_saturation, mapping_lookup_latency, percent_reconnects_after_ip_rotate. Add alert if nat_pool_saturation > 70% for 5m.
Fiona P (arch): compliance callout: for customers with SOC2/PCI needs, require per-tenant SGs and static IPs. We'll flag on contract.
Gabe S (neteng): rough rollout plan: 1) implement lease service + API, 2) add ip_affinity flag in control plane, 3) enable per-tenant ENI support behind feature flag, 4) canary with 5 customers in same AZ, 5) flip to prod.
Hannah T (sre): add emergency fallback: control plane can set ip_affinity=ephemeral to consolidate traffic if we detect NAT exhaustion. That requires careful customer notification.
Fiona P (arch): action items: Gabe run perf spike + PR for lease service, Hannah add alerts + runbook, I'll wire contract gating and update docs.
Gabe S (neteng): PR opened: gh/infra/lease-service #128, ETA for initial review tomorrow.
infra-bot: build #4123 finished: tests passed. Canary schedule window ready. :white_check_mark:
Hannah T (sre): tagging @oncall-network for visibility.
Fiona P (arch): thanks team, will capture decision in RFC follow-up with example failure modes and rollback steps. Leaving thread as single source for rollout conversation.
